paths.description: Homepage and news dashboard: entry template, navigation, match strip, poll, ads and notification prompt.
Representative article/detail template, selected from the homepage lead story.
Representative section/listing template for scanning current news.
Primary scores-and-fixtures journey, including date and competition controls.
Primary search journey using an Arabic club query.
Representative unknown URL to assess HTTP failure and recovery.

findings.summary: Persistent prompts and advertising obscure or displace core content.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a fixed notification prompt/ticker across the bottom; the desktop entry also dedicates both side rails and large blank blocks to advertising.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not show notification solicitation on load. Defer it until a user gesture and remove or collapse persistent overlays so content remains unobstructed.

findings.summary: Advertising and persistent chrome dominate the reading surface.
findings.evidence: The 1440px screenshots show side-rail ads, large reserved ad gaps and a bottom ticker; the article headline does not begin until roughly 570px down the viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce above-the-fold ad inventory, reserve only compact slots, and prioritize the lead content and article heading in the first viewport.

findings.summary: Search does not complete its core journey predictably.
findings.evidence: Navigating to /search?q=الأهلي redirected to the homepage and displayed “no search results” while unrelated homepage articles were listed beneath it.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the search route and query visible, return actual matching results, and present a distinct useful empty state only when no matches exist.

findings.summary: The not-found state offers no recovery path.
findings.evidence: The unknown URL renders the raw ASP.NET “Server Error in / Application” page with framework versions and no links, search, retry or route back to content.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace framework error output with a branded 404 that explains the state and offers home, search and popular-section recovery actions.

findings.summary: Mobile LCP is outside the good range on primary templates.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured homepage LCP 4.30s and article LCP 3.71s, with performance scores 0.74 and 0.76.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP image/content, reduce render-blocking dependencies and delay nonessential advertising and analytics until after core content.

findings.summary: Core carousel controls and imagery lack accessible names or alternatives.
findings.evidence: axe found two critical unnamed carousel buttons and a missing-alt image on both homepage and article; the image probe counted 59 images without alt values.
findings.suggestedFix: Name every icon-only control and provide meaningful alt text, or empty alt/role=presentation for decorative imagery.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but baseline security headers and cookie flags are missing.
findings.evidence: The header primitive found no CSP, HSTS or nosniff; the cookie audit found 8 of 9 cookies without Secure and several SameSite=None cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a measured CSP, HSTS and nosniff policy, and mark all HTTPS cookies Secure with the narrowest viable SameSite/HttpOnly settings.

findings.summary: Tracking and advertising execute across a very broad third-party surface.
findings.evidence: The tracker scan found 24 third-party origins and 9 known tracker domains; the HAR attributes 105 requests and 1.96MB to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit vendors, remove duplicate analytics, gate nonessential tracking behind valid consent, and batch/minimize retained event data.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: No frame protection, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy was present, in addition to missing HSTS and CSP.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; consider Trusted Types after CSP is stable.

findings.summary: HTTP failure handling exposes a raw framework error.
findings.evidence: The tested missing route returns a bare ASP.NET 404 containing framework versions and no navigation or recovery control.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle 404/5xx at the application edge with useful, accessible recovery states and no implementation disclosure.

findings.summary: Background advertising and analytics work is disproportionate to the content load.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 105 of 157 requests and 1.96MB; multiple GTM/gtag files and advertising auctions start during initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Deprioritize and conditionally load background vendors, remove duplicate tags, and stop work when content is hidden or consent is absent.

findings.summary: Third-party media and scripts consume most transferred bytes.
findings.evidence: Third-party traffic is about 81% of transfer weight; the HAR includes a 193KB advertising video plus large ad and analytics scripts before user request.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, defer media until view or intent, disable autoplay advertising media and enforce vendor cache budgets.

findings.summary: The site stays light when the user requests dark mode.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is visually identical to the light capture; the preference probe reports color-scheme: normal and the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and retint text, surfaces, controls and advertising surrounds under prefers-color-scheme, following the dark-mode guide.

findings.summary: Dismissible UI is built from ad-hoc controls rather than semantic overlay primitives.
findings.evidence: DOM probes found zero dialog, popover and details elements despite the visible notification prompt and custom close controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal permission education or popover for transient prompts, with declarative actions, focus management and light dismiss.

findings.summary: Some controls are undersized or lack clear keyboard semantics.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe found 19 of 210 visible interactive targets below 24px in one dimension; axe also found two unnamed carousel buttons.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase control hit areas toward 44 CSS px, add accessible names, and preserve a strong :focus-visible indicator for every custom control.

findings.summary: Main-thread blocking remains material in mobile lab runs.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 343ms TBT on the homepage and 306ms on the article even though the separate warm trace did not record a long task.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile mobile startup, split or defer noncritical work, and schedule advertising/analytics initialization after the core rendering path.

findings.summary: The request graph is large and script-heavy.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 157 requests and 2.42MB transferred, including 38 scripts totaling 1.52MB and numerous parser-inserted stylesheet candidates.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, defer noncritical styles and scripts, and sequence ad dependencies after primary content.

findings.summary: Large amounts of shipped JavaScript and CSS are unused.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 672KiB of unused JavaScript and 17KiB of unused CSS; multiple analytics tags and ad libraries dominate the waste.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate analytics tags, conditionally load advertising integrations, and split template-specific CSS/JS.

findings.summary: At least one primary action fails minimum color contrast.
findings.evidence: axe reported a serious color-contrast violation on #PollVote and marked 11 additional homepage nodes for manual contrast review.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust action colors to meet WCAG AA in every state and add automated contrast checks to the component palette.

findings.summary: Heading and list structure is inconsistent across templates.
findings.evidence: The homepage has no h1; axe found article heading-order, list and listitem violations, and probes show heading sequences beginning at h4.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide one descriptive h1 per template, keep heading levels sequential, and use valid ul/ol and li structures for carousels and related stories.

findings.summary: Several controls remain too small for reliable touch use.
findings.evidence: At 360px the page reflows without overflow, but the probes counted 19 undersized homepage targets and 9 undersized match-page targets.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target boxes and spacing while retaining the successful no-overflow mobile layout and user-scalable viewport.

findings.summary: Primary pages log runtime and network errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured failed service-worker registration and repeated 429 failures for the manifest, menu, carousel and page scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Stop rate-limiting required page assets, make service-worker registration failure-tolerant, and monitor first-party resource errors in production.

findings.summary: Image metadata and sizing are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 14 images without dimensions and 8 oversized images; Lighthouse found a poll image displayed at an incorrect aspect ratio.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio, preserve source aspect ratio, and serve responsive sources at their rendered size.

findings.summary: Some navigation controls are not crawlable links.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed crawlable anchors; the homepage includes javascript:void(0) links, and template probes found multiple empty/unlabelled href anchors.
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for actions and real href URLs for navigation, with descriptive text or accessible names.

findings.summary: Installability and offline support are unreliable.
findings.evidence: A standalone manifest exists, but Lighthouse repeatedly received 429 for it and service-worker registration failed because firebase-messaging-sw.js returned 429.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve the manifest and service worker reliably, separate notification messaging from offline caching, and provide a tested offline fallback for core news.

findings.summary: RTL intent is implicit and CSS relies overwhelmingly on physical directions.
findings.evidence: All templates set lang=ar but omit dir=rtl; the homepage CSS probe counted 534 physical directional declarations and only 1 logical-property occurrence.
findings.suggestedFix: Set dir=rtl on the root and migrate reusable layout rules to inline/block logical properties.

findings.summary: Asset delivery still wastes bytes despite broad WebP adoption.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 19 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, 33 without srcset, 8 oversized and 12 legacy-format images.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold media, add responsive srcset/sizes, correct dimensions and migrate remaining photographic assets to modern formats.

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences are not handled explicitly.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-contrast: more the probe still reports the normal scheme, while CSS inspection found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations that preserve boundaries, focus indicators and scrollbar visibility.

findings.summary: Primary cross-document navigation lacks a consistent transition.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition opt-in on the homepage, so navigation from the entry page cannot participate in a cross-document transition.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enable cross-document View Transitions on both source and destination templates, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Site chrome does not adapt to scroll state.
findings.evidence: Mobile screenshots show a fixed header and fixed ticker, while CSS inspection found no scroll-state container/query or progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state-aware CSS to reduce persistent chrome after scrolling and preserve orientation with a lightweight progress/current-section cue.

findings.summary: Reusable components depend on viewport-oriented CSS rather than container-aware adaptation.
findings.evidence: Across four templates, CSS probes found no @container rules even though the same match/news cards appear in wide and narrow placements.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards and match widgets containment and size-aware @container rules, retaining viewport fallbacks where needed.

findings.summary: The page uses a deprecated browser API and produces DevTools issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported deprecated Attribution Reporting usage and inspector issues in both tested primary templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated attribution calls and resolve the underlying browser Issues panel entries rather than suppressing them.

findings.summary: Date presentation mixes Arabic content with fixed English labels.
findings.evidence: The Arabic matches page visibly renders MON/TUE/WED/THU beneath dates, indicating fixed labels rather than consistently locale-aware formatting.
findings.suggestedFix: Format date/day labels with Intl.DateTimeFormat for the active locale and keep machine values location-agnostic.

findings.summary: The search input lacks an accessible label and input assistance metadata.
findings.evidence: Across templates the visible search input has no associated label or aria-label and an empty autocomplete value.
findings.suggestedFix: Give search a persistent accessible name and use the search autocomplete token where appropriate.

taskList.title: Replace the broken search and raw framework error states with complete, recoverable journeys
Reduce, consent-gate and defer advertising, tracking and duplicate analytics
Deploy baseline security headers and secure cookie attributes
Fix names, alternatives, headings, contrast and target sizing across shared components
Improve mobile LCP and the critical resource path
Move article and homepage content ahead of ad gaps and persistent chrome
Make the manifest, service worker and first-party assets reliable under load
Build a preference layer for dark and high-contrast modes
Optimize responsive images and correct intrinsic sizing
Modernize RTL and locale handling with root direction, logical CSS and Intl dates
Use semantic overlay controls, container queries and crawlable links
Add progressive cross-document and scroll-state navigation enhancements
